notes.taxonomy: The evidence LEVEL is decided by the observation alone. NOT_COVERED when the candidate supports the Answer proposition; L0 when the candidate has no observed object for the same predicate and direction; L1 when the candidate has at least one observed alternative object; L2 only with a machine-checkable EvidenceProof.
notes.l0: L0 needs no rule. It is absence-only observation under the Open World Assumption: the pinned snapshot records nothing for the key on that candidate.
notes.l1: L1 needs no rule either. A different observed object IS a positive value contrast, including under a multi-valued predicate, because L1 reports an observed contrast and not an established impossibility. This corrects the Prompt-8F policy, which required an active scoped rule before a positive alternative could reach L1.
notes.exclusion_basis: The strength of the exclusion argument is reported on a separate axis. L1 + NONE is a positive observed contrast only. L1 + SCOPED_EMPIRICAL is the same contrast, additionally annotated by an ACTIVE local empirical single-valued rule. L2 + FORMAL_PROOF is a verified exclusion. An annotation may be preferred when ranking equally strong rationales and may never change a level.
notes.l2: L2 requires a machine-checkable proof carrying premises, a conclusion and an ontology or schema source. The l2_rules list below is EMPTY for the Journal-2 pilot: DBpedia infobox properties (the dbp: namespace) carry no functional, maximum-cardinality, disjointness or negative-assertion declarations, and none is available offline. Declaring one here would fabricate exclusion evidence. Zero L2 cases in the pilot is therefore the correct reported outcome, not a gap to be filled.
notes.temporal_l2: Temporal L2 additionally requires real statement-level qualifiers. DBpedia infobox facts have none, so qualifier_status is UNAVAILABLE_IN_SOURCE and temporal L2 is unreachable on this source by construction.
notes.okuhara_inference_templates: Okuhara 2025 uses P(x,y) AND P(y,z) -> P(x,z) and P(x,y) AND capital(z,y) -> P(x,z) to add panoramic bypass links. Those are link-creation heuristics, not negative-evidence rules and not statement qualifiers, and they are deliberately NOT used as L2 exclusion rules here.

empirical_single_valued_derivation.scope_note: The scope is the Answer plus the complete ranked candidate pool of the Prompt-8C selected class, as serialized by Prompt 8D. It is a LOCAL, EMPIRICAL scope: the rule says nothing about the predicate outside this class and nothing about DBpedia as a whole, and it is never described as universal functionality.
empirical_single_valued_derivation.minimum_support_note: Support is the number of distinct entities in the scope observed with at least one object for the key. Five is the declared default. Because an active rule now only annotates exclusion_basis, the threshold cannot move a fact between L0 and L1; every derived candidate is published with its support, maximum observed cardinality, violation count and activation status.
empirical_single_valued_derivation.violation_note: A violation is an entity in scope observed with two or more CANONICALLY DISTINCT objects for the key. Canonical equivalence is applied first, so a redirect pair does not count as two values.
empirical_single_valued_derivation.inactive_direction_note: For an IN key the observed cardinality is an IN-DEGREE: how many other articles in the local pool happen to point at the entity with that predicate. A maximum in-degree of one across a handful of entities reflects how thinly the snapshot covers those articles, not a property of the predicate. IN-direction candidates are therefore derived and published as PROPOSED_NOT_ACTIVE.

annotation_rules_note: Curated scoped annotation rules would be listed here. The pilot declares none: every annotation it uses is DERIVED at run time by empirical_single_valued_derivation above, from the frozen Prompt-8D observations.

functional_conflict_requirements: a trusted functional or maximum-cardinality declaration from ontology_source
an observed alternative object on the candidate
canonical inequality between the Answer object and the candidate object
no equivalence and no parent-child support relation between them
temporal_conflict_requirements: actual statement-level qualifiers on both statements
l2_rule_schema.non_functional_predicates_note: birthPlace, almaMater, knownFor, influenced, author, products and similar predicates are NOT treated as functional merely because one value happens to be observed for one entity.
